title: Council Signal: How Measurement Feeds AI Governance — Council of AI Explained
context: 2026-09-01 engine cycle — answer-first page connecting the Council Signal measurement framework to real governance decisions; aligns to the 14-axis board and the verified measurement credential
body: Council Signal is the measurement backbone that turns AI governance from a paperwork exercise into an evidence-backed discipline. Instead of asking whether an AI system is safe or compliant in the abstract, Council Signal asks: what did the measurement actually show, and was it signed by an independent verifier? The framework works across four layers. First, a measurement axis — one of the fourteen axes on the Council of AI board, each representing a dimension where model behaviour matters for governance: care, determinism, privacy, affect, governance posture, and so on. Second, a benchmark bank — a curated set of test items that exercise that dimension, drawn from public and proprietary benchmarks and run with a consistent protocol. Third, a measurement pass — a sweep across every model in the manifest for that axis, producing a signed attestation of where each model landed. Fourth, a governance decision — the measurement is fed into a compliance gate, a procurement checklist, or a risk register so the answer to is this model acceptable is not based on a vendor claim but on independently verifiable evidence. The signal is verified measurement credential: the output of a measurement pass carries an Ed25519 signature from a recognised signing node, so any downstream auditor can confirm the numbers were not altered. Council Signal is not a prediction — it tells you what happened, not what will happen — and it is not a certification. It is the measurement layer that makes certification auditable.
